title: AEE detection, analysis, and remediation registry
principles: Use deterministic detection and verification whenever possible.
Route only allowlisted contextual questions to an AI specialist.
Require synchronized full-page visual, DOM, and accessibility-tree evidence for AI analysis.
Mark every AI-produced conclusion or suggestion clearly and preserve its audit trail.
Never treat missing, unsupported, or contradictory evidence as a pass.

entries.title: Missing or unsuitable accessible name
entries.applicability: Interactive controls and form elements whose accessible name is absent, generic, duplicated, or inconsistent with the visible purpose.
deterministicDetection: Run pinned axe-core rules at each meaningful checkpoint.
Compute the accessible name and compare it with the rendered role and visible text.

ai.purpose: Suggest a concise, context-specific name when deterministic checks can prove a name problem but cannot author the wording.

verification: Rerun the same journey and prove the computed name is non-empty and unique enough for the task.
Match visible purpose, DOM, accessibility tree, and screen-reader output.
Confirm keyboard activation and resulting user outcome are unchanged.

entries.title: Image purpose and text alternative
entries.applicability: Rendered images, SVGs, icons, and CSS images whose purpose depends on their relationship to surrounding content or controls.
deterministicDetection: Identify rendered non-text content and its exposed alternative or hidden state.
Flag mechanically provable missing alternatives and role conflicts.

ai.purpose: Classify an image as decorative, informative, functional, or complex and draft text only when page context is required.

verification: Confirm the rendered image, nearby content, DOM treatment, accessibility tree, and spoken output express the same purpose.
For decorative images, verify they are absent from the accessibility tree and spoken output.

entries.title: Visual and semantic heading structure
entries.applicability: Pages where typography, spacing, grouping, or repeated regions imply a hierarchy that may differ from the semantic outline.
deterministicDetection: Extract the complete semantic heading outline and structural relationships.
Record visual typography and grouping signals without deciding meaning.

ai.purpose: Compare the full visual hierarchy with the full DOM and accessibility-tree outline when the intended relationships require contextual judgment.

verification: Re-extract the full outline after the fix.
Confirm visual grouping, DOM hierarchy, accessibility tree, and screen-reader heading navigation agree.

entries.title: Text and component color contrast
entries.applicability: Visible text, icons, focus indicators, controls, and meaningful graphics whose foreground and background colors can be sampled or inferred.
deterministicDetection: Use axe-core where foreground and background colors can be determined.
Calculate WCAG contrast ratios from resolved colors; never let a model estimate the ratio.
Select the closest passing supplied design token using deterministic color-distance and contrast calculations.

ai.purpose: Locate complex rendered foreground and background regions or explain brand intent when deterministic extraction is inconclusive.

verification: Recompute the exact contrast ratio from the final rendered colors.
Verify default, hover, focus, active, disabled, and error states that apply to the component.

entries.title: Keyboard operation and activation
entries.applicability: Every visible or inferred interactive candidate, including elements discovered visually even when semantics are missing.
deterministicDetection: Drive Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, arrows, Escape, and role-specific keys through the active keyboard lane.
Record document.activeElement, deep active element, aria-activedescendant, visible focus, and accessibility-tree focus after every meaningful action.
Compare the observed outcome with the scenario's authorized expected outcome.

ai.purpose: Keyboard operability and focus movement are verified from recorded behavior, not inferred by AI.

verification: Repeat the same role-aware key sequence in an isolated active lane.
Confirm focus moves only when required and the user outcome matches pointer activation.
Require explicit authorization before destructive or financial actions.

entries.title: Hover and keyboard-focus equivalence
entries.applicability: Content or controls revealed, changed, or made available on pointer hover, keyboard focus, or activation.
deterministicDetection: Run hover and keyboard paths in separate active browser contexts.
Capture synchronized before and after evidence for hover, focus, Enter, and Space when appropriate to the role.
Compare available user outcomes rather than requiring identical implementation events.

ai.purpose: Equivalent behavior is decided from traces and outcomes; AI does not substitute for exercising both paths.

verification: Verify hover content is dismissible, hoverable, and persistent where WCAG requires it.
Verify the equivalent information or control is reachable and usable by keyboard and represented consistently to the screen reader.

entries.title: Focus management after interface changes
entries.applicability: Dialogs, route changes, inserted or removed content, validation, async updates, composite widgets, and other meaningful state changes.
deterministicDetection: Record focus and aria-activedescendant before and after every meaningful action.
Detect loss of focus, hidden focused elements, and focus outside an opened modal.
Record live-region and screen-reader output separately from focus movement.

ai.purpose: Focus movement and announcements are observable state. AI may explain evidence later but cannot decide or cause the movement.

verification: Confirm only the active input driver moves focus.
Do not both move focus and announce the same update unless the interaction pattern requires both.
Match focus, visible context, DOM, accessibility tree, and spoken output after the action.
